result.summary: Do not ship: password changes no longer revoke existing sessions, leaving compromised cookies usable.

findings.title: Restore session revocation on password change
findings.body: Updating only password_hash preserves session_secret. A stolen triggarr_session cookie issued before the password change still passes AuthMiddleware at triggarr/web/middleware.py:146–148: validate_session checks only the signature and 30-day expiry, never the password hash. An attacker therefore retains authenticated access after the owner changes their password. No replacement revocation check guards this path.
findings.recommendation: Restore atomic session_secret rotation with the password update and reissue the acting user's cookie under the new secret. Verify that a second device's pre-change cookie is rejected.

next_steps: Restore revocation and run the existing password-change rotation and session-eviction tests in tests/test_auth_routes.py and tests/test_auth_integration.py.
